notes: fallback: no LLM synthesis ran (no Claude API credentials), so every archetype and number is hand-written in backend/pipeline/personas.py (ARCHETYPES); none is measured, and calibration should tune them.
The numbers are the builder's judgement, informed by facts in the cited pages: Time Out for the venue mix and opening patterns, ONS Time Use and TfL for daily timing.

returningProb is high for daily routines (residents, commuters, office and shift workers) and ~0 for tourists; lightingSensitivity is highest for night-time and unfamiliar visitors; storePrefs, stopsPerTrip, dwellMinutes and entryKinds are per-archetype judgement.
Time Out London: robots.txt checked; 3 of 3 Shoreditch guide pages fetched (scrape cache data/raw/timeout/) and cited.
Reddit r/london, r/AskLondon, r/londonsocialclub: not collected; REDDIT_CLIENT_ID and REDDIT_CLIENT_SECRET are not set (the PRAW path runs once both are).
Google Maps, Yelp and TripAdvisor reviews: not collected; their terms of use forbid scraping.
ONS Time Use and TfL open data: cited as the public basis for daily timing (work and meal times, rail peaks, Friday/Saturday night trains); not fetched or fitted.
share = share of weekday arrivals into the area; on Sat/Sun weight it by weekendMultiplier and renormalise.
activeHours = arrival weight by clock hour, normalised to sum 1 for each persona.
weekendMultiplier applies to Sat/Sun clock days, so Friday-night hours after midnight count as Saturday.
Implied returning share of weekday arrivals (sum of share x returningProb): 0.58.
morning-commuter: weekday rail peaks 07-09 and 17-19 through Shoreditch High St (TfL); coffee to go, often no stop at all; weekdays only, so weekend 0.25
office-worker: works in the area's offices: lunch peak 12-14 and after-work 17-19 (ONS daily routines); the same routine every weekday, so returning 0.85
remote-worker: laptop workers in cafes 09-17 with long dwell (Time Out: a late-night bar serves them breakfast from 8am; a pay-by-the-hour venue runs 8am-6pm); daytime, so lighting barely matters
local-resident: lives nearby and walks in: evening grocery and off-licence runs 17-21, more at weekends; habit over lights; the most regular group
tourist: visitors for markets, museums, galleries and food 10-19 (Time Out area guide), busiest at weekends; one-off (0.02 covers multi-night hotel stays); a lit front signals open to strangers
weekend-shopper: Londoners at markets and independent shops 10-17, mostly Sat/Sun (Time Out: Columbia Road flower market Sundays 8am-3pm, Brick Lane Market); several shops plus a cafe
after-work-drinker: office crowd in bars 17-23 (Time Out: a 5-8pm happy hour; a pub that fills with nearby tech workers from 7pm); bar first, takeaway later; regular haunts, so returning 0.55
evening-diner: dinner 18-22 with a drink before or after (the Time Out area guide lists destination restaurants); more at weekends; occasional repeat visits

night-owl: club-goers arriving 21-02, busiest at weekends (Time Out: XOYO draws crowds every weekend; late-night bars and a pub-club with a late licence); Fri/Sat night trains (TfL); pre-drinks, the club, then late food (takeaway 0.9); drawn to lit, open fronts
late-shift-worker: hospitality, cleaning and care staff finishing 22-02 or starting 05-07; quick food on the way home by night bus; regular shifts, so returning 0.8
student-creative: art and design students and studio workers on loose hours 11-01 (Time Out area guide: galleries, gig venues, arty pubs); cheap cafes, bars and takeaways; half are regulars

sources.label: NESO Carbon Intensity API (CC BY 4.0), London regionid 13, half-hourly estimates 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-30
NESO Carbon Intensity API (CC BY 4.0), London regionid 13, half-hourly estimates 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-14
DESNZ ND-NEED 2026, England and Wales (published 30 Sep 2026): median electricity intensity by building use from metered 2024 consumption
CIBSE TM46:2008 Energy benchmarks (typical electricity and fossil, kWh/m2 GIA per year)
Clark (2013) What Colour is Your Building?, Appendix C, Tables C.4, C.6 and C.10: reproduces the TM46:2008 rows used here
DESNZ QEP table 3.4.2: prices of fuels purchased by non-domestic consumers in the UK, including CCL (published 29 Sep 2026)

notes: carbonGPerKwh: live. Mean of 1344 half-hourly London (regionid 13) estimates, 2026-09-17 to 2026-10-14 (UTC days), grouped by Europe/London clock hour: lowest 94.8 g at 13:00, highest 187.8 g at 18:00. Regional values are NESO model estimates (the API's 'forecast'; no regional 'actual' is published).

cafe: 160 kWh/m2/yr (ND-NEED 2026 Hospitality median, metered 2024); open 07:00-18:00 (11 h) on 365 days = 4015 h/yr (assumption); standby share 0.2 (display chillers and fridges stay on overnight; the espresso machine is on a timer) -> 0.0322 kWh/m2 per open hour, 0.0064 closed; 100 m2 on an open day = 43.8 kWh before facade lighting.

restaurant: 160 kWh/m2/yr (ND-NEED 2026 Hospitality median, metered 2024); open 12:00-23:00 (11 h) on 365 days = 4015 h/yr (assumption); standby share 0.15 (only the walk-in fridge and freezer run while kitchen and dining room are off) -> 0.0338 kWh/m2 per open hour, 0.0051 closed; 100 m2 on an open day = 43.8 kWh before facade lighting.

takeaway: 310 kWh/m2/yr (TM46 Small food store: TM46 has no takeaway category and this is the closest all-electric, refrigerated counter-service format); open 11:00-23:00 (12 h) on 365 days = 4380 h/yr (assumption); standby share 0.3 (fridges, freezers and drinks chillers on a small floor area) -> 0.0544 kWh/m2 per open hour, 0.0163 closed; 100 m2 on an open day = 84.9 kWh before facade lighting.

bar: 160 kWh/m2/yr (ND-NEED 2026 Hospitality median, metered 2024); open 16:00-00:00 (8 h) on 365 days = 2920 h/yr (assumption); standby share 0.25 (cellar cooling and bottle fridges run around the clock) -> 0.0365 kWh/m2 per open hour, 0.0091 closed; 100 m2 on an open day = 43.8 kWh before facade lighting.

shop: 108 kWh/m2/yr (ND-NEED 2026 Shops median, metered 2024); open 10:00-19:00 (9 h) on 365 days = 3285 h/yr (assumption); standby share 0.2 (a mix of corner shops with drinks chillers and non-food shops with little left on) -> 0.0247 kWh/m2 per open hour, 0.0049 closed; 100 m2 on an open day = 29.6 kWh before facade lighting.

offlicence: 310 kWh/m2/yr (TM46 Small food store); open 08:00-23:00 (15 h) on 365 days = 5475 h/yr (assumption); standby share 0.4 (glass-door drinks chillers dominate the load and never switch off) -> 0.0457 kWh/m2 per open hour, 0.0183 closed; 100 m2 on an open day = 84.9 kWh before facade lighting.

club: 150 kWh/m2/yr (TM46 Entertainment halls, the closest category for a late-night music venue); open 22:00-03:00 (5 h) on 156 days = 780 h/yr (assumption); standby share 0.1 (cellar cooling and bar fridges against a large sound, lighting and ventilation load; 3 club nights a week) -> 0.0951 kWh/m2 per open hour, 0.0095 closed; 100 m2 on an open day = 65.6 kWh before facade lighting.

kWh/m2 derivation: E = annual electricity intensity, H = typical open hours per year, f = standby share (closed-hours load / open-hours load). open = E / (H + f x (8760 - H)) and standby = f x open, so a store kept to its typical hours uses exactly E a year; dividing E by H alone would count the closed-hours load twice. Each extra open hour costs (open - standby) per m2.

Cross-check, CIBSE TM46:2008 typical electricity (kWh/m2 GIA/yr): Restaurant 90 and Bar or pub 130 (both assume gas cooking and heating: fossil 370 and 350), General retail 165, Small food store 310, Entertainment halls 150. TM46 Restaurant would put a 100 m2 cafe at ~25 kWh/day, below an all-electric espresso cafe, so cafes, restaurants and bars use the metered ND-NEED hospitality median (ND-NEED publishes no split within hospitality).

Benchmarks cover a building's whole electricity use including its lighting. Facade and window lighting (lightingKw) is added on top, so stores with lights on most hours model slightly above their benchmark.

Floor area bases differ: ND-NEED divides by VOA floor area, TM46 by gross internal area, and map.json floor areas come from footprints. Clark (2013) puts the spread between measurement bases at up to ~25%, inside the benchmark uncertainty.

lightingKw (assumption: LED fittings on a typical small shopfront, independent of floor area): off = 0; low 0.25 kW = illuminated fascia sign 0.10 + window display dimmed 0.15; high 0.60 kW = sign 0.10 + window display at full 0.30 + facade wall-washers and canopy 0.20. Older halogen fittings would draw 2-3x more.

priceGbpPerKwh: flat £0.3201/kWh, the midpoint of DESNZ QEP 3.4.2 2025 annual non-domestic electricity prices incl. CCL, excl. VAT: Very Small band (0-20 MWh/yr) 34.93 p/kWh and Small band (20-499 MWh/yr) 29.09 p/kWh, because the modelled independents straddle the 20 MWh/yr boundary. These are average delivered prices (standing charges spread per kWh), so the unit rate a saved kWh avoids is somewhat lower. DESNZ publishes no time-of-day split, hence flat. DESNZ flags the Very Small series as subject to revision.

EPC: the non-domestic EPC register (epc.opendatacommunities.org) now redirects to get-energy-performance-data.communities.gov.uk, whose API needs a GOV.UK One Login bearer token (checked 2026-10-15; this build has none), so it is not used. Non-domestic EPCs are modelled asset ratings, not metered use, so metered ND-NEED medians are the closer source.

fallback describes the carbon profile only: True means the API could not be used and the snapshot was written. Intensities, lighting and price are published figures plus the assumptions stated here in every build.

notes: Units: sim agents per hour (expected values; sample e.g. Poisson per hour), not real people. Scale: 1 sim agent ~ 34 real arrivals.

Scale derivation: station exits per weekday / weekend day (TfL NUMBAT 2025, mean of calendar days) x the share walking into the map area (assumption): Liverpool Street 189,726 / 120,404 x 20% = 37,945 / 24,081; Shoreditch High Street 11,495 / 10,023 x 90% = 10,345 / 9,021; rail arrivals into the area 48,291 per weekday and 33,102 per weekend day. Assumed station share 40% of all arrivals into the area gives 120,727 real arrivals per weekday; weekday sim total fixed at 3,500 (BUILD_NOTES budget 2,000-4,000 a day for the 1.5 km x 1.5 km map); weekend total 2,399 follows the measured weekend/weekday ratio of those rail arrivals, 0.69.

Station entries: hour-of-day = each station's own exits (people arriving; quarter-hour bands summed to hours), TfL traffic days (05:00-05:00) mapped to calendar days; the stations split the station budget by their arrivals into the area, and several entries of one station split its share equally. Into-area shares (assumptions): Liverpool Street 20%: the station sits ~150 m inside the south edge and ~300 m inside the west edge; most of its commuters walk south and west into the City (Bank, Bishopsgate south, Leadenhall, Moorgate), outside the map, while Broadgate's offices north of the station, Spitalfields and the walk up Bishopsgate to Shoreditch are inside: one exit in five assumed to head into the area; Shoreditch High Street 90%: the map origin, 700-800 m (about a 10-minute walk) from every edge, so nearly every exit stays in the area; 10% assumed to walk on past the edges or change to a bus.

Night services: TfL lists Shoreditch High Street on the Windrush Night route (Unified API); NUMBAT exits 01:00-05:00 by night: Liverpool Street: Mon 19, Tue-Thu (each) 31, Fri 492, Sat 703, Sun 16; Shoreditch High Street: Mon 0, Tue-Thu (each) 0, Fri 76, Sat 108, Sun 0. Late station arrivals therefore sit in the 00-04 hours of the weekend profile (Sat/Sun mornings) and are ~0 on weekday nights.

Street entries (assumption): hourly arrivals at street edges are not measured here; timing = 70% weekday / 60% weekend exit timing of the stations' arrivals into the area plus 30% / 40% night-time-economy walk-ins (weekday 11:00-01:00, peak 17-23; weekend 10:00-04:00, peak 20-24). Split across street entries by the width of the street each sits on: e1 14 m, e2 8 m, e3 8 m, e4 8 m, e5 8 m, e6 8 m, e7 8 m, e8 12 m, e9 8 m, e10 8 m, e11 8 m, e12 8 m, e13 14 m, e14 5 m, e15 12 m, e16 12 m, e17 8 m, e18 8 m, e19 8 m, e20 8 m, e21 14 m, e22 10 m, e23 8 m, e24 8 m, e25 8 m, e26 8 m, e27 14 m, e28 12 m, e29 8 m, e30 14 m, e31 8 m, e32 8 m, e33 8 m, e34 10 m, e35 8 m, e36 8 m, e37 14 m, e38 10 m, e39 14 m, e40 8 m, e41 14 m, e42 8 m, e43 8 m, e44 10 m, e45 3 m, e46 8 m, e47 10 m, e48 8 m, e49 8 m, e50 8 m, e51 8 m, e52 8 m, e53 14 m, e54 8 m, e55 8 m, e56 8 m, e57 8 m, e58 8 m, e59 8 m, e60 10 m, e61 8 m, e62 8 m, e63 8 m, e64 14 m, e65 8 m, e66 8 m, e67 6 m.

Club nights: one per club store, nights thu/fri/sat, hours from map.json defaultHours when they describe a night (open from 18:00, close after midnight by 08:00), else 22:00-03:00 (assumption; club events are not scraped). Club-goers are NOT in entryPoints: the sim adds `capacity` club-goers per club night; capacity is already in sim agents (do not rescale). capacity = floor area / 0.5 m2 per person (Approved Document B) x 60% typical fill, clamped 150-1500 real (500 without floor area), x scale 0.0290: c1 22:00-03:00 (map hours), 216 real -> 6 agents; c2 22:00-03:00 (map hours), 720 real -> 21 agents; c3 22:00-03:00 (map hours), 515 real -> 15 agents; c4 22:00-03:00 (map hours), 448 real -> 13 agents.

returningShare and returningPoolSize (estimate; open question in the spec): commuters = arrivals in the TfL AM peak band 07:00-10:00 (31% of weekday, 7% of weekend arrivals) plus 25% of all other arrivals assumed regulars (residents, regular diners and drinkers, club regulars); weekly mix = 0.44. Pool = share x busiest daily total / 0.9 (a regular arrives on ~9 of 10 days) = 1717.

Checked 2026-10-15, not used: TfL crowding API (/crowding/910GSHRDHST returns isFound=false); ONS Time Use Survey tables (OTUS, March 2024) give daily minutes per activity with no hour-of-day split, so hour-of-day comes from NUMBAT; TfL BUSTO bus demand files are 55-125 MB (over the download cap); Resident Advisor, Dice and Eventbrite are not scraped (terms).

PLACEHOLDER, NOT MEASURED: 5 of 5 venues (measured=false) are hand-written shapes of the hourly pattern Google Popular Times typically shows for the venue type, not data for these venues. They cannot validate the sim: calibration error and report confidence must leave them out.

Scale: 0-100 = share of the venue's busiest hour of the week (Popular Times scale). weekday = mean of the Mon-Fri calendar days, weekend = Sat-Sun; an hour after midnight belongs to the next calendar day (Fri 01:00 counts as Saturday), as in StoreStats.
s12 Quaker Street Coffee & Bubble Tea (cafe) is the cafe nearest the station; placeholder (weekday commuter rush 08-10 and lunch, weekend brunch peak 11-14).
s27 Rochelle Canteen (restaurant) is the restaurant nearest the station; placeholder (lunch 12-14 and a bigger dinner peak 19-21, busiest on Saturday).
s45 Pavilion Bar (bar) is the bar nearest the station; placeholder (after-work rise from 17:00, latest and busiest on Friday and Saturday nights).
c3 Village Underground (club) is the club nearest Bagel buzz; placeholder (open Thu-Sat 22:00-03:00, peak 01-02 on Friday and Saturday nights).
s29 Bagel buzz (takeaway) is the takeaway nearest a club (Village Underground, 79 m); placeholder (lunch, dinner 18-21 and an after-club peak 02-04 on Friday and Saturday nights).
Popular Times needs a paid API key: BESTTIME_API_KEY and OUTSCRAPER_API_KEY are not set (SerpAPI is key-gated too and not wired in), so no venue was measured.

London Datastore checked 2026-10-15 (all 1306 datasets): no open hourly high-street footfall for Shoreditch, Hackney or Tower Hamlets. Closest: Google Mobility by Borough (daily % change, All Rights Reserved, ended Oct 2022), the COVID-19 Mobility Report footfall series (daily, London-wide) and LTDS 'Trips made in London by time of day' (London-wide weekday trip starts). GLA High Streets Data Service footfall is not in the open catalogue (only its boundaries, dataset 2rq4w).

calibration.note: No measured targets yet: all calibration shapes are placeholders, so the sim is uncalibrated and report confidence is capped.
